Position Summary The University of Central Arkansas (UCA) is seeking a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor (9-month appointment) to join the School of Nursing. This on-campus role is designed for a doctorally prepared (DNP or PhD) Family Nurse Practitioner who will shape the next generation of nursing professionals. The successful candidate will lead innovative educational programs, conduct scholarly research, and contribute to a supportive, inclusive academic environment. Learn more at: www.uca.edu/nursing Job Duties and Responsibilities This tenure track position focuses on teaching, curriculum development, assessment and evaluation, collaboration and mentorship. The faculty member will facilitate student learning, engage in research and scholarship, focus on continuous professional development and provide institutional, professional and community service. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities As a tenure-track faculty, you will translate intricate clinical data into digestible, evidence-based instruction. You will ground your teaching in the current realities of healthcare policy and ethics, ensuring students are equipped to navigate the systemic challenges of modern healthcare.Key Responsibilities: Curriculum Innovation: Design and deliver high-impact programs utilizing active learning and high-fidelity simulations. Mentorship & Leadership: Guide novice nurses and colleagues through the nuances of clinical judgment and professional identity. Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Thrive within academic teams to drive institutional excellence and adapt to evolving accreditation standards. Scholarly Contribution: Advance the profession through reflective practice, original research, and advocacy for healthcare equity. Qualifications & Skills: Clinical Mastery: Advanced knowledge of nursing science and delivery systems. Instructional Excellence: Proven ability to apply educational theory to clinical complexity. Dynamic Communication: Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to lead and inspire. Adaptability: A commitment to lifelong learning and the integration of emerging healthcare technologies.
